scenarios.title: Prepare an export area beside retained evidence
scenarios.summary: Use a safe aligned gap in an existing GPT disk; allocation and formatting are separate decisions.
scenarios.objective: On /dev/vda add exactly one new partition named staging, 8–12 MiB inclusive, with a Linux data hint and an aligned start. Initialize its actual content as ext4 with label export. Preserve the supplied archive partition and /keep.txt, every other disk and all unrequested space; do not create GPT again or add extra partitions.

concepts.title: Read the supplied media first
concepts.text: A disk is the whole supplied virtual device. A partition is one named range inside its table. Read the status: Read-only, In use or Existing data to preserve means it is not spare writable media. The applied disk table and retained file details are inspection facts, not draft fields.

concepts.title: Inclusive sectors and alignment
concepts.text: Here each sector holds 512 bytes and 1 MiB is 1048576 bytes. A range includes both ends, so bytes=(end-start+1)*512. Each supplied alignment is 2048 sectors: choose a start divisible by 2048. GPT reserves sectors 0..33 and the final 33 sectors; the last usable sector on these 131072-sector disks is 131038. No extent may overlap another.

concepts.title: A type hint is not content
concepts.text: Linux data and Linux swap are partition type hints. Adding a partition chooses an extent and a hint; it does not create a filesystem or swap signature. Choose the actual partition number shown in the applied table, then explicitly initialize blank content as ext4 or swap. A name or a hint alone cannot pass a content requirement.

concepts.title: Labels, UUIDs and preservation
concepts.text: A label is a short human-readable name for the actual filesystem or swap area. A UUID is an identity; any valid unique identity satisfies these tasks. Leave the UUID field blank for this simulator's persistent deterministic generator, or provide an explicit lowercase UUID. Existing nonblank signatures and file contents must remain unchanged.

concepts.title: Drafts, applied state and honest recovery
concepts.text: Fields are unapplied drafts. Add, Create GPT and Initialize content are explicit native actions. Check evaluates the applied configuration against every required row and preservation rule. A correct applied result stays correct when an unfinished draft is edited. This subset cannot delete, resize, overwrite or undo a valid allocation: use Reset practice, or reset the affected assignment, then replay the intended actions. Inspect protection before committing.

concepts.title: Preparation is not activation
concepts.text: The tools are simulator controls, not commands executed on your computer. ext4 creation here models a 4 KiB-block capacity and identity, not a real filesystem image. Swap initialization prepares a header; activating it with swapon, mounting filesystems and editing fstab are outside this model. Real formatting can destroy data and these simulator refusals are not general real-tool safeguards.

lesson.description: Aspen practice has a 4 MiB archive on /dev/vde1. Add sample in a different free interval, 3–5 MiB, then initialize /dev/vde2 as ext4 with label sample. The smaller sample and its separate /keep.txt are ungraded. After success, add extra at 20480..22527 to see preservation fail.

scenarios.title: Deliver prepared storage without disturbing retained data
scenarios.summary: Complete an existing blank filesystem extent and choose separate media for swap while preserving the full supplied inventory.
scenarios.objective: Initialize the existing handoff partition /dev/vda1 as ext4 with label dispatch; keep its 10 MiB extent and the archive /dev/vda2 with /keep.txt unchanged.
